process_observations.observation: The blocked -> running -> built path worked exactly as the status machine documents: the operator re-claimed the step with a recorded reason, no plan field was hand-edited, and all four runs (running, blocked, running, built) are preserved in steps[M4-S01].runs[].

The block produced a skill improvement rather than a workaround: commit 5b206697a moved a rule from 'this shape is wrong' to 'this shape is wrong on the default calendar', updated gotcha #1 and the worked example to match, and left gotcha #6's UNVERIFIED marker standing where the evidence genuinely stops.

No metadata changed between the blocked run and the built run, so the step's outcome turned entirely on a rule the build does not own — which is the shape a checker-policy block should have when it is real rather than an artefact defect.

The checker's INFO line asks whether anything expecting business-hour pauses is attached to the always-open calendar, and the answer at M4 is that nothing reads it at all — the 24/7 promise is carried operationally by M4-S04's businessHoursSource None entry, so the calendar is a placeholder for a Severity 1 entitlement process that does not yet exist.

Neither agent's Wave 10 report pair under docs/reports/ was written on either run, because the invocation constrained writes to the build directory; all four build-scoped envelope pairs were written and all validate.

Two things the step is built on remain unsettled and are marked rather than resolved: the midnight-pair semantics, which gotcha #6 still calls UNVERIFIED because the api_meta line the operator supplied documents the value and not the pair, and Acme's holiday list, which no clarification question ever asked for.
The step is built and untested; its checker, XML, manifest and manual tests are all outstanding, and the manual one is the only assertion that all three calendars are present and named.
